verdict: NOT READY to accept real customer health information
scope: Deduplicated union of every finding, condition and evidence gap preserved in this workspace.

runs.name: Baseline repository audit
runs.note: Full report, 18-finding register and questionnaire matrix.

runs.name: Freebuff Pre-Underwriting Audit Prompt pass
runs.note: The archive records that no separate second finding report was present. No unique IDs were available to merge; this pass is represented by the conditions list.

runs.name: Qwencloud audit
runs.note: 18 prior findings reconfirmed at the same commit; 6 new findings.

findings.prior_title: Public submission accepts a fabricated questionnaire snapshot
findings.title: Public submission accepts a fabricated questionnaire snapshot
findings.verification: Runtime reproduced against the real validateDraft
findings.affected: Questionnaire fidelity, reviewer evidence, held data
findings.launch_impact: Blocks launch
findings.summary: The public function checks answer shape and vocabulary but never checks the question against an approved bank.
findings.observed: The probe accepted MED-11 (held HIV) as approved, RES-05 (held visa/green-card number), INVENTED-99 with invented source text and 'Past 99 years', a zero-answer payload, an invented questionnaire version, and a client-invented not_applicable disposition that hides a row from the summary. It rejected duplicate IDs, more than 400 answers, marketing without a phone and non-self relationship.
findings.consequence: Fabricated questions, altered windows and held sensitive answers can enter the immutable case; a reviewer cannot tell the record was never approved.
findings.remediation: Ship a canonical server-side bank; rebuild source text, timeframe, status, reviewStatus and disposition from it; reject unknown IDs, mismatches, held rows and stale acknowledgements.
findings.acceptance_test: Forged MED-11, INVENTED-99, changed-timeframe and zero-answer payloads return 422 and write no row.

findings.prior_title: Consent evidence is client-asserted and not validated server-side
findings.title: Consent evidence is client-asserted and not validated against server policy
findings.classification: Confirmed defect; marketing part is a pre-enable gate
findings.verification: Runtime reproduced against the real validateDraft
findings.affected: Consent separation, TCPA evidence, privacy acknowledgement
findings.launch_impact: Blocks launch; independently blocks enabling marketing
findings.summary: The server requires intake and privacy consent objects with granted:true but trusts their IDs, wording, versions, timestamps and any extra records; it has no channel or seller policy.
findings.observed: The probe accepted marketing_call and marketing_text with no channel or seller configured, an unknown consent ID, a duplicate privacy acknowledgement, textVersion '1999-01-a' with different wording, a 2027 grantedAt with completedAt before startedAt, an arbitrary acknowledgement ID/version, and a marketing numberAuthorized that did not match the lead phone.
findings.consequence: The case can contain evidence the customer never saw the stated wording or consented to an unoperated channel; the privacy acknowledgement can be fabricated.
findings.remediation: Use server constants for consent IDs, versions and wording hashes; a server-owned channel/seller policy; reject duplicates, unknown IDs, mismatches and future timestamps; store client and server receipt times separately.
findings.acceptance_test: Forged marketing while disabled, wrong version/text, duplicate/unknown ID and future timestamps return 422; a valid draft returns 201 with both times.

findings.prior_title: The questionnaire does not preserve seven source windows and has no approved row
findings.title: The questionnaire replaces seven source windows and has no source-verified row
findings.classification: Confirmed deviation plus missing named approval
findings.verification: Recomputed from the audited bank and reconciliation data
findings.launch_impact: Blocks launch; primary blocker
findings.summary: All 92 rows have sourceVerified false, yet 87 are reviewStatus approved and shown. Seven rows replace a source window, 11 change wording, 19 source items are partly collected and 9 are out of scope.
findings.observed: MED-10 current -> past 5 years; AVI-04 next 2 years -> next 12 months; AVO-01 past/next 2 years -> past 5 years; RES-02 source 5-year residence + 2-year travel -> past 5 years outside US; RES-03 next 2/24 months -> next 12 months; MIL-01 current active duty -> ever served; MIL-03 current/planned deployment -> past 12 months. 37 rows are listed for sign-off (34 with a non-matching verdict or flag, plus three compound splits that need confirmation); no row has a named sign-off.
findings.consequence: Customers are asked different questions from the controlled source, including narrower future-travel and wider past-avocation windows; there is no defensible approved questionnaire version.
findings.remediation: Obtain a named owner/counsel/underwriting decision for each of the 37 rows; restore the source window or record an approved deviation with name/date; set sourceVerified only then; bump the version and regenerate the report.
findings.acceptance_test: A signed table covers all 37 rows; check:bank passes; branch tests cover restored rows; sourceVerified is true only with evidence.

findings.title: Client-supplied crisis flag and review flags are not re-derived server-side
findings.verification: Runtime reproduced against the real validateDraft; portal path statically traced
findings.affected: Current-crisis triage, reviewer safety, queue prioritisation
findings.launch_impact: Blocks launch
findings.summary: The server accepts crisisDisclosure and flags from the client instead of deriving them from the submitted MH-05 answer. A forged payload can answer MH-05 Yes while setting crisisDisclosure false and flags empty.
findings.observed: The probe accepted an MH-05 Yes answer with crisisDisclosure:false and flags:[]; submit-case stores draft.crisisDisclosure in the crisis_disclosure column and the payload flags; PortalPage uses crisisDisclosure for the Safety disclosure badge and CaseReview uses the payload flags for Review flags.
findings.consequence: An attacker or buggy client can suppress the urgent queue badge and crisis panel for a customer who disclosed current self-harm thoughts, delaying human review.
findings.remediation: Derive crisisDisclosure from the canonical MH-05 answer on the server; derive flags from the answer set; ignore or reject client flags that contradict answers; test MH-05 Yes with false flags.
findings.acceptance_test: A payload with MH-05 Yes and crisisDisclosure:false is either rejected or stored with crisis_disclosure true and an urgent server-derived flag; no client-supplied flag can remove it.

findings.prior_title: Branch-closed details survive into the submitted record
findings.title: Branch-closed details survive into the submitted record
findings.verification: Runtime reproduced with the real engine
findings.affected: Answer integrity, branch behaviour, reviewer view
findings.launch_impact: Blocks launch for the answer-integrity gate
findings.summary: Changing a parent answer does not clear child answers; toSubmittedAnswers emits fields for every row, including those whose disposition is not_asked.
findings.observed: With MH-01 Yes and four MH-02 fields, then MH-01 No, MH-02 became not_asked but still carried four fields; CaseReview renders fields and details regardless of disposition.
findings.consequence: A customer who withdraws an answer still sends the withdrawn health detail and the reviewer sees it under 'Not asked'.
findings.remediation: Delete hidden descendants when visibility changes; omit fields/details for not_asked; render no components for not-asked rows; test nested branches.
findings.acceptance_test: Parent flip leaves no hidden child fields in state, payload or portal.

findings.prior_title: No submission idempotency; ambiguous retries duplicate cases
findings.title: No submission idempotency; ambiguous retries duplicate cases
findings.verification: Statically demonstrated; no HTTP load test
findings.launch_impact: Blocks launch for the delivery-reliability gate
findings.summary: Every POST inserts a new case; the only uniqueness is the server-generated reference. The client sends no idempotency key and has no abortable timeout.
findings.observed: A lost response after a successful insert, a retry or a rapid double submission creates a second case. A reference collision retries with a new reference, not the original request.
findings.consequence: Duplicate cases and reviewer work after timeouts or double clicks.
findings.remediation: Per-draft idempotency key, unique index, replay returns the original receipt, abortable client request reusing the key.
findings.acceptance_test: Concurrent and timed-out submissions create exactly one case with one reference.

findings.prior_title: Notification retry can duplicate sends and has no row claiming
findings.title: Notification retry can duplicate sends and has no row claiming
findings.verification: Statically demonstrated
findings.launch_impact: Blocks launch for the delivery-reliability gate
findings.summary: The submit function sends before updating status; the retry worker selects queued/failed rows without FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, a lease or a claim state, and sends before updating.
findings.observed: A failed status write after provider acceptance leaves the row queued and the next retry sends again; overlapping cron invocations can both send; the customer response can say accepted when the database write failed.
findings.consequence: Duplicate reviewer emails and conflicting status evidence.
findings.remediation: Provider idempotency key, row lease/SKIP LOCKED, sending state before call, message-ID reconciliation, persisted receipt.
findings.acceptance_test: Crash-after-accept and overlapping-worker tests produce exactly one email.

findings.prior_title: Delivery webhook accepts replay/out-of-order events and can regress status
findings.title: Delivery webhook accepts replay/out-of-order events and can regress status
findings.verification: Statically demonstrated
findings.launch_impact: Blocks launch for the delivery-evidence gate
findings.summary: email.sent/delivery_delayed map to accepted and email.delivered to delivered, with no event ID, timestamp tolerance or monotonic transition; a later email.sent overwrites delivered.
findings.observed: The endpoint compares a shared secret directly and has no raw-body signature, replay window or event dedupe. A replayed or delayed event is accepted.
findings.consequence: The portal can regress delivery evidence or show contradictory status.
findings.remediation: Verify provider signature over raw body, timestamp tolerance, event-ID dedupe, no downgrade from delivered, message-ID reconciliation.
findings.acceptance_test: Forged, replayed and out-of-order events cannot create or regress delivery evidence.

findings.prior_title: Deployment configuration is absent from the repository
findings.title: Deployment configuration and retry schedule are absent from the repository
findings.verification: Repository inspection
findings.launch_impact: Blocks deployment and launch
findings.summary: README instructs verify_jwt=false and says to keep the flags in the repo, but no supabase/config.toml or cron/schedule definition exists.
findings.observed: A by-the-repo deployment hits the default JWT protection on the public endpoint, and the retry function has no scheduler evidence.
findings.evidence: README.md:222-234; LOVABLE.md; no supabase/config.toml; no cron definition
findings.consequence: Anonymous submissions can fail before reaching the handler, or notifications stay queued forever.
findings.remediation: Commit the three function JWT settings and a documented schedule; verify a deployed 401-to-201 transition and one cron tick.
findings.acceptance_test: A clean deployment accepts an anonymous non-customer submission and the retry worker runs on schedule.

findings.title: No adult/self or jurisdiction verification
findings.verification: Static; runtime probe accepted a ZZ state
findings.launch_impact: Blocks launch unless the business accepts the risk in writing
findings.summary: The lead form collects no age/DOB; relationship is a constant self; the server accepts any 2-40 character state and treats relationship:self as proof.
findings.observed: A minor or third party can complete the interview; an invented state ZZ is stored. The DOB question arrives later and is not used for an age gate.
findings.consequence: The specification's adult-self boundary is a UI assertion, not a control.
findings.remediation: Capture DOB/adult attestation before health questions; compute age server-side; validate state against the US list; reject non-self; test 17-year-old, ZZ and third-party payloads.
findings.acceptance_test: A 17-year-old, ZZ state and non-self relationship are rejected.

findings.prior_title: Held sensitive source questions are shown verbatim to customers
findings.title: Held sensitive source questions are shown verbatim to customers
findings.verification: Statically demonstrated in the review component
findings.launch_impact: Blocks launch for the sensitive-question gate
findings.summary: The review screen expands 'Questions held for human review' and renders each held row's sourceText, including HIV, suicide-attempt, immigration and visa-number wording.
findings.observed: The five held rows (ID-04, MED-11, MH-06, RES-04, RES-05) are excluded from the interview but their full source text is rendered in the customer review panel.
findings.consequence: The product surfaces sensitive content it says it withholds and puts identity-document-adjacent wording in front of every visitor.
findings.remediation: Show a count and generic topics or internal references, not source text; keep the full list in the reviewer/coverage record; test the customer DOM.
findings.acceptance_test: Held wording is absent from the customer DOM and public bundle under the chosen policy.

findings.title: Marketing revocation and suppression are promised but unimplemented
findings.verification: Static; no outbound marketing channel is enabled
findings.affected: Consent withdrawal, suppression enforcement, TCPA operations
findings.launch_impact: Pre-enable gate; blocks enabling marketing, not the current disabled-channel build
findings.summary: The messaging terms promise action within 10 business days and describe STOP/email withdrawal, but there is no revocation route or job; the contact_suppressions table is never read by application code.
findings.observed: The table exists with reviewer select only; no outbound code checks it. MessagingTermsPage makes the 10-business-day promise. Marketing is off by default, so no active outreach is occurring.
findings.evidence: src/pages/MessagingTermsPage.tsx:37-42; supabase/migrations/0001_pre_underwriting.sql:199-224; grep finds no application read of contact_suppressions
findings.consequence: Once a call/text channel is enabled, a STOP or revocation could fail to propagate and the published 10-day commitment would not be evidenced.
findings.remediation: Add a revocation path and operator procedure; check suppression before every outbound attempt; log receipt and action; test STOP, email withdrawal and a revoked number.
findings.acceptance_test: A revocation creates a suppression record and an outbound attempt is blocked with auditable timing.

findings.title: Reviewer MFA is enrollment-only; no policy requires an AAL2 session
findings.verification: Statically demonstrated; live session behaviour not tested
findings.launch_impact: Blocks launch for real customer data
findings.summary: The portal accepts any Supabase session whose user is in reviewers; is_reviewer() checks membership only. Nothing in the client or the RLS policies requires auth.jwt()->>'aal' = 'aal2'.
findings.observed: useReviewerAuth reads session.user.email without checking authenticatorAssuranceLevel, the portal gate uses email !== null, and every reviewer policy calls is_reviewer() only. Supabase does not auto-enforce AAL2 at the API gateway; its documented enforcement is an RLS/gateway check. A password-only aal1 session for an MFA-enrolled reviewer therefore still selects cases.
findings.consequence: A stolen reviewer password bypasses the second factor and exposes every case, including current-crisis disclosures.
findings.remediation: Require aal2 in the reviewer RLS policies or a trusted gateway, and make the portal refuse an aal1 session with a clear step-up prompt; test with a password-only session.
findings.acceptance_test: A password-only reviewer session sees zero cases and cannot call the review/correction RPCs; after TOTP step-up the same session succeeds.

findings.title: No retention, deletion, backup or incident-response control is implemented
findings.verification: Repository inspection; no live project available
findings.affected: Data lifecycle, deletion requests, breach readiness
findings.launch_impact: Blocks launch for real customer data
findings.summary: The README and launch checklist say retention/deletion and incident response are not implemented; cases have no delete policy and no expiry job, while the customer is told they can ask for deletion.
findings.observed: README line 29 says the retention/deletion job is not implemented. The cases table has no delete policy. PrivacyPage and PermissionStep promise correction or deletion on request, and CaseReview says retention follows the documented schedule, but no schedule, deletion procedure, backup expiry or incident runbook exists in the repository.
findings.consequence: Real health data would be retained indefinitely, a deletion request could not be honored reproducibly, and a breach would have no documented response or backup boundary.
findings.remediation: Approve a retention schedule; add a controlled deletion/expiry procedure and audit entry; document backup expiry and incident response; test a labelled case deletion and restore path.
findings.acceptance_test: A labelled case can be deleted under the approved procedure, the deletion is audited, backups expire on schedule and the incident runbook names an owner and contact path.

findings.prior_title: Privacy acknowledgement records the wrong notice version
findings.title: Privacy acknowledgement records the wrong notice version
findings.verification: Statically demonstrated
findings.launch_impact: Nonblocking independently; fix with QW-02
findings.summary: The displayed privacy version is 2026-10-a, but buildConsentRecords stamps the privacy record with the shared consent version 2026-10-b.
findings.observed: The privacy record cannot prove which notice version the customer saw.
findings.consequence: The case links the customer's acknowledgement to a different document version.
findings.remediation: Use a per-purpose noticeVersion and stamp the privacy record with PRIVACY_PRACTICES_VERSION.
findings.acceptance_test: The stored privacy record carries the displayed privacy version.

findings.prior_title: Body cap counts characters, not bytes, and is applied after reading when Content-Length is absent
findings.title: Body cap counts characters, not bytes
findings.verification: Runtime reproduced with the real handler
findings.launch_impact: Nonblocking hardening
findings.summary: MAX_BODY_BYTES is 512 KB, but the post-read check is raw.length > MAX_BODY_BYTES; a multibyte body can exceed 512 KiB while passing.
findings.observed: A 424,063-character / 824,063-byte body passed the character check and reached service configuration instead of returning 413.
findings.consequence: The stated byte cap is not enforced; the platform's own limits bound the damage.
findings.remediation: Measure TextEncoder byte length or stream with a byte counter; reject before full buffering where possible.
findings.acceptance_test: A multibyte body above 512 KiB returns 413 before validation or service configuration.

findings.prior_title: Rate limiting is per-instance and keyed by a spoofable header
findings.title: Rate limiting is per-instance and keyed by a spoofable header
findings.verification: Statically demonstrated
findings.launch_impact: Nonblocking at low volume with monitoring; relevant before public launch
findings.summary: The limiter is an in-process Map of 10 requests per 10 minutes keyed by the first X-Forwarded-For or cf-connecting-ip.
findings.observed: A caller can rotate the header or hit a fresh instance; the code already says a WAF or durable limiter belongs in front.
findings.consequence: An attacker can fill the reviewer queue and cause operational load.
findings.remediation: Durable or WAF limiting keyed on trustworthy client identity; alert on submission volume.
findings.acceptance_test: Header rotation and a second instance do not bypass the durable limit.

findings.title: not_sent cases are never retried
findings.verification: Statically demonstrated
findings.launch_impact: Nonblocking only if no real case is submitted before provider configuration; otherwise operational blocker
findings.summary: The retry worker selects only queued and failed; a missing provider or portal origin yields not_sent and zero attempts, which is never selected again.
findings.observed: Cases submitted before provider setup remain visible in the portal but can never be notified by the worker.
findings.consequence: The reviewer may never be alerted.
findings.remediation: Add an operator re-notify action for not_sent, or include it once a provider is configured, with an audit entry.
findings.acceptance_test: A not_sent case can be re-queued and produces exactly one notification.

findings.title: Confirmation says the case was queued when notification was not sent
findings.verification: Statically traced in the not_sent path
findings.launch_impact: Nonblocking; fix before launch
findings.summary: The confirmation header always says 'Your answers are saved and queued for review', even when receipt.notification.state is not_sent; the timeline below correctly says no notification was attempted.
findings.observed: Preview and provider-unconfigured submissions return not_sent, so the header and timeline contradict each other.
findings.consequence: A customer can believe the reviewer was notified when no message was sent.
findings.remediation: Make the header conditional on notification state; say saved but not sent and give the next step; test preview/not_sent.
findings.acceptance_test: No 'queued' copy appears unless state is queued/accepted, and the header matches the timeline.

findings.prior_title: Stale and misleading documentation and UI counts
findings.title: Stale and misleading documentation and UI counts
findings.verification: Recomputed from the audited files
findings.launch_impact: Nonblocking; fix before launch
findings.summary: Several counts and claims are stale: 56-row references, 76 'source questions', 31 unanswered items, and Not applicable listed as implemented though never rendered.
findings.observed: site.ts and reconciliation.ts say 56 rows while the bank has 92; the landing page labels 76 approved core rows as source questions though the inventory has 113 and 85 traced; README says no row collapses lookbacks while seven replace windows; the README walkthrough records 31 unanswered while fresh engine data has 73 visible/unanswered on an empty interview; NOT_APPLICABLE_OPTION is defined but not offered; LAUNCH-GATES marks gates 3, 4, 6 and 7 Implemented although the server still trusts the client snapshot/acknowledgement, injection was not tested and MFA is not enforced.
findings.consequence: Reviewers and the owner can overstate coverage; customers see a misleading source-question count.
findings.remediation: Generate counts from one source; relabel 76 as approved core rows or show 113/85; remove 56; implement or remove Not applicable; replace inherited walkthrough numbers with a dated ledger.
findings.acceptance_test: A generated count check passes and no stale count remains in customer or reviewer copy.

findings.title: Dependency and CI supply-chain exposure
findings.verification: npm audit and workflow inspection
findings.launch_impact: Nonblocking
findings.summary: npm audit reports 4 advisories (3 moderate, 1 high): Vite 5.4.21 and react-router-dom 6.30.6. CI actions are tag-pinned and npm ci runs lifecycle scripts.
findings.observed: No app path was found that exposes the react-router advisories; the Vite high advisory primarily affects the dev/build toolchain. CI has contents: read only.
findings.consequence: Known toolchain advisories; a compromised action tag or install script is a supply-chain path.
findings.remediation: Update Vite/react-router to patched releases, pin actions to SHAs, consider npm ci --ignore-scripts, review install scripts.
findings.acceptance_test: No high advisory remains and CI actions are SHA-pinned.

findings.prior_title: Deno dependencies are unpinned and there is no lockfile
findings.title: Deno dependencies are unpinned and there is no lockfile
findings.verification: Repository inspection
findings.launch_impact: Nonblocking
findings.summary: deno.json maps @supabase/supabase-js to a major range; tests import jsr:@std/assert@1; the documented command uses --no-lock and no deno.lock is tracked.
findings.observed: A future CI run or deployment can resolve different versions without a repository change.
findings.consequence: An upstream break is invisible until it happens; builds are not reproducible.
findings.remediation: Pin exact versions, commit deno.lock and run tests with the lockfile in CI.
findings.acceptance_test: A clean CI run uses the committed lockfile and pinned versions.

findings.title: Live portal never records an 'opened' access entry
findings.verification: Statically demonstrated
findings.launch_impact: Nonblocking; fix with access logging
findings.summary: case_review_log allows 'opened' and the preview sample includes it, but no live code path calls record_case_review('opened') when a reviewer loads a case.
findings.observed: getCase loads the case and its log without writing an opened entry; CaseReview only calls recordReview for marked_reviewed and requested_clarification. A reviewer can read a case without leaving access evidence.
findings.consequence: The access record cannot show who opened a sensitive case, only who changed its status.
findings.remediation: Record one opened entry per reviewer/case load (idempotent per session) through the RPC, and show it in the review log; test deduplication and failure handling.
findings.acceptance_test: Loading a case as a reviewer adds one opened entry with actor and time; reload does not spam duplicates.

findings.prior_title: Immutability trigger covers the payload but not all evidence metadata
findings.title: Immutability trigger covers the payload but not all evidence metadata
findings.classification: Confirmed narrow scope; no reviewer exploit
findings.verification: Isolated PostgreSQL replay
findings.launch_impact: Nonblocking hardening
findings.summary: The trigger protects payload, reference, submitted_at and questionnaire_version, but crisis_disclosure and residence_state are not protected and the service role can change them.
findings.observed: The PGlite replay changed crisis_disclosure as the service role without tripping the trigger; reviewer column grants blocked the same change.
findings.consequence: A privileged operator or service-role bug could change queue triage metadata without detection.
findings.remediation: Include derived evidence columns in the immutable set, or document why they are mutable; test with the service role.
findings.acceptance_test: A service-role change to crisis_disclosure or residence_state is rejected or explicitly audited.

conditions.title: Approve the questionnaire before customer use
conditions.requirement: Every bank row has a named owner/counsel/underwriting decision; the seven replaced windows are restored or explicitly approved; sourceVerified is true only with evidence; QUESTIONNAIRE_VERSION is bumped and the report regenerated.
conditions.acceptance: A signed 37-row decision table exists; check:bank passes; no held row is offered; every count in customer/reviewer copy is generated from the bank.

conditions.title: Make the server authoritative for the snapshot and crisis state
conditions.requirement: The public endpoint rebuilds every answer from a canonical bank and rejects held, unknown, altered, incomplete and stale rows; crisis_disclosure and review flags are derived from the answer set, never trusted from the client.
conditions.acceptance: Forged MED-11/INVENTED-99/zero-answer/not-applicable payloads return 422; MH-05 Yes with a false crisis flag fails closed or stores true.

conditions.title: Make consent evidence server-owned
conditions.requirement: Consent IDs, versions, wording hashes, seller/channel policy and receipt time are server-owned; forged marketing/privacy evidence is rejected; the privacy version matches; revocation and suppression are enforced before any channel is enabled.
conditions.acceptance: Wrong version/text, duplicate/unknown IDs, disabled-channel marketing and future timestamps return 422; STOP/withdrawal creates a suppression and blocks outbound.

conditions.title: Preserve answer integrity and the adult/self boundary
conditions.requirement: Branch-closed details are purged from state, payload, summary and portal; adult/self and US-state rules are server-enforced; not_applicable is approved or removed.
conditions.acceptance: Parent flip leaves no hidden fields; 17-year-old, ZZ and third-party payloads are rejected; every branch test passes.

conditions.title: Protect review and submission integrity
conditions.requirement: A forged or stale acknowledgement is rejected server-side; edits invalidate the prior confirmation; one draft creates at most one case.
conditions.acceptance: Arbitrary ack/version is rejected; edit then old ack is rejected; double submit/timeout creates one case.

conditions.title: Make delivery reliable and evidence trustworthy
conditions.requirement: Idempotency, claimed/leased retries, provider idempotency, signature-verified/deduplicated/monotonic webhooks, committed JWT/schedule config and honest not_sent copy.
conditions.acceptance: Concurrent/timeout submissions create one case; crash/overlap sends one email; replayed/out-of-order events cannot change status; confirmation matches state.

conditions.title: Verify secure reviewer access
conditions.requirement: Live RLS is verified with anonymous, authenticated non-reviewer and reviewer; AAL2 is required; opened access is logged; a forwarded reference alone is denied.
conditions.acceptance: Password-only session sees zero cases and cannot call RPCs; after step-up it succeeds; opened entry exists; forwarded reference denied.

conditions.title: Implement data lifecycle and incident controls
conditions.requirement: Retention/deletion, backup expiry, incident response, revocation/suppression, mailbox ownership and provider settings are documented, implemented and tested.
conditions.acceptance: Labelled deletion is audited; backups expire; incident runbook names owner/contact; STOP blocks outbound; provider settings reviewed.

conditions.title: Close customer and provider exposure
conditions.requirement: Held source text is not shown to customers; privacy version is correct; customer/reviewer counts are accurate; bundle/logs/URLs/email/provider settings are re-checked for health data.
conditions.acceptance: Held wording absent from customer DOM/bundle; privacy record matches displayed version; generated count check passes; no health data in logs/email/URLs.

conditions.title: Obtain legal and clinical approvals
conditions.requirement: Counsel approves the entity, privacy notice, intake permission, TCPA disclosure (if any), sensitive-question handling and HIPAA/Texas position; clinical review approves the crisis script.
conditions.acceptance: Signed approvals identify the entity, versions, dates and scope; no 'HIPAA compliant' or 'TCPA compliant' claim is made from this audit.

conditions.title: Complete operational readiness
conditions.requirement: Mailbox ownership, sender domain, provider settings, monitoring, on-call, deployment config and a labelled non-customer end-to-end test are confirmed.
conditions.acceptance: Non-customer case reaches the approved mailbox; reviewer signs in with MFA; one failed delivery is observed and recovered; on-call/contact is documented.

conditions.title: Pin and reproduce the supply chain
conditions.requirement: Dependencies are updated, CI actions are SHA-pinned, install scripts reviewed, Deno dependencies pinned and deno.lock committed.
conditions.acceptance: No high advisory remains; CI uses the lockfile; a clean build resolves the same versions.

conditions.title: Keep real data out until the blockers close
conditions.requirement: The environment remains in labelled preview mode; no real applicant data is accepted until all launch-blocking findings and MC-01..MC-12 are closed.
conditions.acceptance: Written confirmation that the environment accepts fictitious data only; live mode remains off.

evidence_gaps.gap: Migrations, RLS, grants and RPCs verified only in PGlite; no hosted project, schema state, migration history or manual SQL changes inspected.
evidence_gaps.qwencloud_note: Qwencloud PGlite replay expanded to 25 checks; hosted project still unavailable.

evidence_gaps.gap: verify_jwt, environment variables, origin allowlist, cron schedule, timeouts, memory and observed rate limiting not tested.
evidence_gaps.qwencloud_note: Qwencloud confirmed no committed config/schedule; live functions still untested.

evidence_gaps.gap: No Resend key or mailbox access; provider acceptance, delivery, bounce/complaint handling, webhook signature compatibility, sender-domain authentication and inbox receipt unverified.
evidence_gaps.qwencloud_note: Qwencloud probe confirmed recipient allowlist and minimal body; provider/mailbox still untested.

evidence_gaps.gap: No live auth; MFA is an operational instruction, not an enforced application control; session expiry and cache behavior untested.
